title: SAML IdP fingerprint & attribute behavior compatibility + validation suite for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Produce a deterministic compatibility reference and automated validation suite covering SAML behaviors and attribute fingerprints / mappings for major IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping). Goal is to eliminate frequent integration regressions, reduce onboarding time for enterprise customers, and ensure RBAC v2 role assertions and audit events are consistent across IdPs. Scope: attribute naming, NameID formats, signature algorithms, assertion encryption, binding types, group/role claim shapes, default session lifetimes, clock skew tolerance, and edge-case behaviors (e.g., multiple group claims, missing attributes, email vs. principal name). Deliverables: 1) IdP behavior matrix (spreadsheet + narrative); 2) automated test harness with representative SAML responses and example metadata; 3) CI gates that run the validation suite against our SAML assertion parser and the RBAC v2 mapping layer; 4) documentation and runbook updates for the Admin Console and Private deployments; 5) migration notes for customers using legacy RBAC mappings.
acceptance_criteria: IdP behavior matrix completed and reviewed by Security, PM, and Support
Automated validation suite covers 26 canonical scenarios and passes in CI for the SAML parser
RBAC v2 mapping tests assert correct role resolution for at least 3 real-world customer group shapes per IdP
Documentation pages updated with explicit IdP quirks and recommended attribute mappings
Runbook includes reproducible steps to diagnose signature/encryption failures and audit log entries

decision_log: Canonical NameID chosen: prefer 'email' if present, fallback to 'persistent' then 'transient' -- agreed 2026-03-10.
Signature verification: enforce RSA-SHA256 minimum for production but allow RSA-SHA1 in staging for legacy customers (toggle via feature flag).
Group claim normalization: support comma-separated and repeated attributes; normalize to lowercase slug for RBAC v2 mapping.
test_plan: Attribute mapping matrix: validate expected attribute keys from each IdP and map to internal principal fields (email, principal_id, groups, department).
NameID permutations: emailAddress, persistent, transient; tests for missing NameID but present subject confirmation data.
Bindings: HTTP-POST, HTTP-Redirect, Artifact (simulate artifact exchange), and IdP-initiated flows.
Signatures: RSA-SHA256, RSA-SHA1; message vs. assertion signatures; certificate rotation scenarios.
Encrypted assertions: test with AES-256 encrypted assertion and decryption key rotation.
Clock skew: validate behavior with +-300s and +-600s to detect failures and log events.
Multiple group claim shapes: repeated 'groups' attributes, single CSV string, nested JSON in custom attribute.
SCIM provisioning hooks: simulate initial provisioning events and group membership sync anomalies.
RBAC v2 propagation: end-to-end test mapping SAML attributes -> internal roles -> API access allowed/denied and audit event emitted.
Audit logging: assert that signature verification failures, missing required attributes, and role-mapping mismatches generate structured audit entries with request_id and idp_fingerprint.
Compatibility fuzzing: randomized SAML responses to detect parser crashes and unexpected exceptions.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood: run validation suite against staging instances and dogfood teams for 7 days.
2) Beta: enable feature flag for 5 existing enterprise customers and monitor error rate / support tickets.
3) Gradual opt-in: expose IdP compatibility report in Admin Console and invite customers to run their metadata through the validator.
4) Full rollout: enable stricter signature and attribute enforcement by default in production release security-2026.04.
Monitoring: create dashboards for 'saml.signatures.failed', 'saml.attributes.missing', and RBAC mapping errors; set alert on >0.5% error rate sustained for 15 minutes.
Rollback criteria: increase in login failures by >2x baseline for 30m or a customer-reported outage affecting a paying Dedicated account.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-strict enforcement could break legacy customer integrations. Mitigation: staged opt-in and feature flag plus clear rollback path.
Risk: Test suite false positives due to environment cert differences. Mitigation: include test certificate fixtures and a cert-rotation test matrix.
Risk: Missing IdP-specific edge cases (e.g., Ping's unusual NameID handling). Mitigation: partner with Escalations & Support to add customer-reported cases into the suite.
Risk: Audit logs may expose PII if assertions are logged. Mitigation: redact PII fields and include idp_fingerprint and hashed principal identifier instead.
